assertions.reason: The thermostat stays in the bank's cool mode until the period starts.
Nothing is written between the 15:30 cycle (which re-asserted the bank) and the period's start.

At the high-cost period's start (16:15) the bank ends and the comfort band is written once: cool 76 F, so the AC stops (indoor 68.5 F is far below it). Before #1416 this write was heat 68 F on a thermostat without hvac_action.

No mode change at 16:15: the 15:30 bank write (same mode, no hvac_action) counts as 'cool ran', so the comfort-edge settling guard keeps cool. Before #1416 the thermostat was switched to heat here, the furnace armed on a hot day.
No re-send between the bank end and the next cycle.
The regular cycle re-asserts cool 76 F (the 15:30 bank record is 60 minutes old, inside the 120-minute window); before #1416 it re-asserted heat 68 F.
No mode change between the bank end and the 16:30 cycle: cool stays armed.
After the bank no surface claims one (issue #1404).
After the bank the briefing quotes the band write actually made at the period start.

name: tou_home_cool_bank_ends_no_hvac_action_1416
description: Issue #1416: the #1405 bank-end golden on a thermostat that does NOT report hvac_action. A home pre-cooled to 68 F for a 16:15 high-cost period; the bank's mode was set at 14:00 and the 15:30 cycle re-asserted the bank in the same mode. Before the fix nothing recorded that the cool side ran (no hvac_action, and a same-mode write is not a mode change; the 14:00 mode change is outside the 120-minute window by 16:15), so at the period's start the selector armed the nearer edge: heat 68 F, the furnace armed on a hot afternoon. Now every accepted bank write records its side, the settling guard holds cool, and the band write is cool 76 F, the same as on a thermostat that reports hvac_action.

verdict.summary: Without hvac_action, the end of a cool bank keeps cool armed instead of arming the furnace
verdict.observed_behavior: 16:15 and 16:30: cool 76 F, no mode write. On f877c50 (before #1416): 16:15 set_hvac_mode heat + heat 68 F, 16:30 heat 68 F.
verdict.expected_behavior: Occupant view: on a hot day the native side stays armed after the bank and the AC idles; the furnace is not armed 0.5 F under the house temperature.
verdict.effectiveness: Fails on f877c50 and on 2523b71 (5e33f00^): 16:15 set_hvac_mode heat + heat 68 F, 16:30 heat 68 F (rows 16:15 setpoint and mode, 16:30 setpoint, briefing row). Removing the bank write's 'ran' record (the _note_deliberate_command(..., "tou", ...) call in _apply_tou_schedule), or the guard's read of it (minutes_since_deliberate_command in _minutes_since_family_ran), brings that back. Real HA cannot catch this: its thermostat reports hvac_action, and this scenario passes there on the old code too.
verdict.alignment: docs/comfort-edge-selection-spec.md (R3: a TOU bank write counts as 'ran' even when the mode is unchanged, Issue #1416), docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md TOU paragraph and docs/scheduler-spec.md (Issue #1405 bank end).
verdict.user_outcome: If this regressed, a home whose thermostat reports no hvac_action would get the furnace armed at every cool bank's end (heat 68 F on a hot day), the flip-flop the settling guard exists to prevent.
